newsitem.title: USA: SFX says stock drop may be unfounded.
newsitem.headline: SFX says stock drop may be unfounded.

text.p: SFX Broadcasting Inc said Thursday its stock may have dropped recently because of investors' concerns over recent agreements between the radio industry and the Justice Department.
As of Thursday afternoon, the company's stock was down about 3-1/2 to 34-3/4.

SFX, which owns or has under contract 80 stations in 23 markets, said it has an "extremely limited cause for concern" over the Justice Department anti-trust agreements between American Radio Systems Corp and Westinghouse Electric Corp's broadcasting unit.

The company said it believes there are only two likely areas of concern involving its operations and its pending acquisitions. It said neither of those can be resolved "in any way that can be deemed to be detrimental to SFX."

The first is a joint selling agreement in Witchita, Ks., where the company said the payment received by SFX is equal to the cash flow of the station. As such, it said, if the agreement ultimately is scrapped, the effect would be zero.
It did not name the Witchita station.

The second possible area involves the pending swap of its four Long Island, N.Y., stations for Chancellor Broadcasting Co's two Jacksonville, Fla., stations. That transaction was approved in October by the Federal Communications Commission and is awaiting Justice Department approvals.
